terms.definition: The electrostatic attraction between positive and negative ions.
terms.examiner: "Electrostatic attraction" and "oppositely charged ions" are the marks. Do not mention sharing or molecules.

terms.definition: The strong electrostatic attraction between a shared pair of electrons and the nuclei of the bonded atoms.
terms.examiner: Both parts are needed: shared pair, and attraction to both nuclei.

terms.definition: A covalent bond in which both electrons of the shared pair come from one of the bonded atoms.
terms.examiner: Also called a coordinate bond. Show it as an arrow from the atom that donates the pair.

terms.definition: The ability of an atom to attract the bonding electrons in a covalent bond.
terms.examiner: It increases across a period and up a group; fluorine is the most electronegative element.

terms.definition: A covalent bond between atoms of different electronegativity, giving a permanent dipole with δ+ and δ− ends.
terms.examiner: A molecule with polar bonds is non-polar overall if it is symmetrical and the dipoles cancel.

terms.definition: A strong permanent dipole–dipole attraction between an electron-deficient hydrogen atom bonded to N, O or F and a lone pair on a N, O or F atom of another molecule.
terms.examiner: In a diagram show the lone pair, the dipoles, and the hydrogen bond as a dashed line to the lone pair.

terms.definition: Induced dipole–dipole interactions, present between all molecules, which increase with the number of electrons.
terms.examiner: Explain in three steps: electrons move, giving an instantaneous dipole; this induces a dipole in a neighbouring molecule; the dipoles attract.

terms.definition: Electron pairs around a central atom repel one another and get as far apart as possible; lone pairs repel more than bonded pairs.
terms.examiner: State the number of bonded pairs and lone pairs, then the shape and angle. Each lone pair reduces the bond angle by about 2.5°.
